summary: 802.1X reauth storm on office APs causes WireGuard interface to unbind on docked macOS devices
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple employees on docked MacBook Pros in the SF office reported sudden loss of corporate network access while still connected to office SSID. Affected hosts showed WireGuard interface down/unbound for ~10-30s and then re-established, causing brief but frequent service disruptions (git/push failures, IDE remote mounts dropped).

Impact:
- ~18 users intermittently lost access to internal services during peak hours (09:30–11:15 PST).
- Developer workflows (git, ssh, remote editor) impacted; potential data loss risk for unsaved work.

Environment:
- Office SF-1 AP cluster (AP firmware 3.3.8), corporate-8021x SSID (EAP-TLS), edge switching: Catalyst-9300, radius cluster auth01/auth02. Affected clients: macOS 14.2 on MacBook Pro with Thunderbolt docks. WireGuard client via system-level service (wg-quick).

Steps to reproduce (from affected user):
1) Dock MacBook, authenticate to corporate-8021x SSID.
2) Start long-running ssh/git operations.
3) After variable time (1–90 minutes) traffic stalls; network briefly falls back to guest VLAN (no internal routes).
4) WireGuard interface logs show peer removed and re-added.

Relevant logs / evidence:
- macOS kernel logs (sample):
  Mar 12 09:48:11 nbp kernel: io80211: EAPOL timeout for user 0x7f...
  Mar 12 09:48:11 nbp kernel: en0: link state changed to DOWN
  Mar 12 09:48:11 nbp wireguard: wg-quick[1234]: interface wg0: peer X removed
  Mar 12 09:48:22 nbp wireguard: wg-quick[1234]: interface wg0: peer X added
- AP logs show burst of reauth requests from client MACs around 09:48 with EAP failure codes 23/75 (timeout).
- Switch logs: port flaps recorded (link drops) from docking station connected ports during same window.
- Radius logs: short spikes in Access-Request/Reject timings but no clear cert revocation.

Initial hypothesis:
- Docked Macs suffer transient L2 flaps (dock <-> NIC handshake) triggered by AP roaming/firmware issue or by switch UDLD/PoE instability. The L2 flap causes 802.1X reauth on the AP which triggers the client to drop interface and reconfigure; wg-quick interprets the interface down as a reason to remove peers, which causes route teardown. The rebind is flaky and correlates with the symptoms.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- On 2026-03-12 10:05 PST, Support temporarily disabled aggressive 802.1X reauth (reassoc throttle) on SF-1 APs and increased switch port stabilization timer to 3s.
- Instructed affected users to disable auto-suspend on docks and to apply vendor firmware update to docks where available.

Next steps planned (from on-call SRE / Networking):
- Validate AP firmware upgrade path (3.3.8 -> 3.4.1) with networking vendor; schedule maintenance window.
- Add guard to WireGuard systemd unit: PostUp script to reapply routes and a netlink watcher to prevent permanent peer removal on short link drops.
- Add alert for >5 reauth events per minute per AP and for WireGuard interface flap rate >3/min.

Requested follow-ups:
- Networking team to run full port power and UDLD checks on affected switch stack.
- Desktop team to prepare an MDM policy for persistent route reapply workaround for macOS WireGuard clients.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:58 - Support (Aria Kumar): Initial triage with affected user. Observed wg0 remove/add around same time as link down in kernel log. Opening ticket and escalating to Networking.

2026-03-12 10:12 - Networking (Evan Liu): Correlated AP reauth bursts from three nearby APs. Noting AP firmware 3.3.8 has a known roaming bug in release notes. Will test config change to reduce reauth sensitivity.
2026-03-12 10:28 - SRE (Noah Rivera): Applied temporary AP reauth throttle + increased port debounce on switch stack. Observed reduction in events for ~45m. Pushing for vendor firmware validation.

2026-03-12 14:05 - Desktop (Maya Singh): Collected failing host syslogs and Power/Dock firmware versions; found 2 docks at firmware 1.0.3 exhibiting frequent link resets. Users instructed to avoid using those docks until replacement.

2026-03-13 08:42 - Networking (Evan Liu): Confirmed AP vendor has firmware 3.4.1 release addressing reauth storm. Vendor recommends patch and kernel-level fixes; scheduled upgrade during off-hours 2026-03-14 02:00–03:00 PST.

2026-03-14 03:20 - SRE (Noah Rivera): Deployed AP firmware 3.4.1 to SF-1 cluster and applied permanent debounce policy on switch stack. Verified no new reauth storms in 8h window. Implemented systemd PostUp route reapply for wg on macOS package and rolled to pilot group.
2026-03-14 11:05 - Support (Aria Kumar): Users report normal behavior during morning session. Closing incident, creating follow-up tasks for monitoring and desktop MDM rollouts.
investigation_notes: Checked AP and switch timestamps; events align with user-reported outages. Packet captures from afflicted host show EAPOL retransmit storms preceding link down.

Radius server logs do not show authentication failures tied to cert revocation or mis-configuration. The spike patterns and vendor release notes point to AP firmware side-effect under heavy roaming/congestion conditions.

WireGuard behavior: wg-quick removes peers when interface resets. On macOS, the system-level rebind is slower than Linux; combined with user-space timer, sessions can drop longer. We reproduced on test bench by toggling dock link quickly causing wg peer removal.
Tested increasing AP reauth timeout and switch debounce — reduced occurrence but did not eliminate. Firmware upgrade recommended by vendor.
Risk assessment: Medium-high if left unaddressed during peak hours. No data exfiltration or security compromise detected.
resolution_notes: Applied vendor AP firmware 3.4.1 to SF-1 cluster (2026-03-14 02:00–03:00 PST). Release notes indicate fix for aggressive client reauth under high roam. Post-upgrade monitoring window (12h) showed no reauth storms.
Switch stack debounce timers increased to 3000ms to avoid rapid port down/up on dock handoffs. Observed stable port states after change.

Rolled out WireGuard client systemd unit change for macOS package (wg-macos-wrapper): added PostUp to re-add static routes and a small netlink watcher that delays peer removal if interface flaps <5s. Deployed to 10% pilot before org-wide rollout.
Workarounds documented for Desktop: avoid legacy dock firmware, disable aggressive power-save on dock NICs. Desktop team to push MDM settings to enforce route-reapply helper.
Follow-ups created: INT-553211 (watchdog alerts for reauth spikes), INT-553212 (MDM policy rollout for WireGuard route helper).
Status: Resolved on 2026-03-14 after 12h clean monitoring window. Recommend postmortem within 7 days to capture procedural improvements and update runbooks.
